title: John's Idea and Hammond's tribute
summary: Durham says he named John's Idea after Hammond, who did not credit him at the tribute night.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: the critics will know it's his style and I want mine on the cover. But, Stanley, I just want to say one thing. The night, the tribute to John Hammond with Benny Goodman and George Benson and Benny Carter and all those on the air, --

Why was it that John went right to the mike and forgot that I named that tune after him when he was sitting in the audience? When we was rehearsing John's idea? And they asked him, how did it get its title? He said, well, it was a little thing that they just called John's Idea, for some reason. He never did say why. He never did say it was my tune. And the reason I brought it up, because four or five guys called me up about it. Couple of white guys called me, called me the next day, why didn't he say nothing about -- give you credit for that song?

Yeah, that was my number, yeah. And he happened to be sitting in the audience and I never could put a title on the thing, and I was rehearsing it. And I had a little idea for riffs in it, he was going -- and I said, Basie, let's name this John's Idea.
So I said, well, maybe he forgot it or something. But they said, well, they asked him how did it get its title. I said, well, maybe he forgot it.
It was on the music there, right on the music.
There would be -- well, I don't know, you can't -- John's Idea arrangement is Jimmy Mundy.
No, that's my number, and it's paying off pretty good now, too.
That's -- Basie's record was your arrangement.
Yeah. Maybe they made a mistake then.
